answer.text:
On startup, `recoverOnStartup` (`src/db/recovery.ts`) picks up every work item in a startup-relevant state and decides what to do with it. The overall principle, stated in both code and docs: a restart is safe while work is running — runners keep working during downtime and retain their results, and Paws reattaches to the same commands, including in-flight Closeout reviews and answer tasks (`README.md:54`) (`src/core/recovery.ts:76-82`).

Concretely, `decideStartup` (`src/core/recovery.ts`) handles in-flight work by state (`src/core/recovery.ts:93-105`):

1. **Items in the merge queue** keep their place (`keep_place`), provided their run isn't still active; if a merge call may have been in flight (recorded in the `merge_call` table, checked via `mergeCallInFlight` (`src/db/remote-merges.ts:78-80`)), the merge job first asks GitHub whether that call went through before doing anything (`src/core/recovery.ts:95-96`) (`src/db/recovery.ts:42-43`).
2. **A run still active in the lane** (cut short mid-work) re-verifies, as do items whose merge was in progress or whose verifying state was interrupted (`src/core/recovery.ts:94-97`).
3. **A verifying item whose runner still holds its Closeout review or check run** re-verifies and attaches to that runner work; when the shutdown cut short a re-verify, `recoverOnStartup` attaches to the runner's Closeout work itself and skips re-applying the decision (`src/core/recovery.ts:98`) (`src/db/recovery.ts:75-82`).
4. **Other running/verifying items resume once in a fresh session**, from their checkpoint or, without one, from their branch. If the runner holds the work, the resume also reattaches to it [E4:100,105].
5. **If an item was already resumed once after a previous start and still isn't finished**, Paws doesn't restart it silently — it asks in Linear (`ask_restart`) whether to start it again (`src/core/recovery.ts:101-102`) [E1:58-60,92-98].

Resumes are staggered (`STARTUP_RESUME_SPACING_MS` spacing via `nextResumeAt`), several parked-item conditions skip work (e.g. a pending capacity-wait job, pending answers or transient retries), and downtime doesn't count against open runner leases up to `offlineBudgetMs` [E1:44,52-64,85].

The README summarizes the same behavior: Paws reattaches to the same commands after startup, including in-flight Closeout reviews and answer tasks (`README.md:54`).

This is based on 5 source ranges in 5 files, not the whole repository. Asking again with mode "deep" can follow the remaining leads.

answer.text:
On startup, Paws runs `recoverOnStartup` (src/db/recovery.ts), which makes one decision per work item found in the startup states — `awaiting_input`, `running`, `verifying`, `recovering`, `merge_queue` — and applies each decision, with the batch wrapped in one transaction (`src/db/recovery.ts:41-101`) (`src/db/decisions.ts:17-20`) (`src/db/recovery.ts:31-37`). The decisions come from `decideStartup` in src/core/recovery.ts, which encodes the policy for items that were mid-work when the process went down (`src/core/recovery.ts:75-106`):

1. **Merge-queue items keep their place.** An item in `merge_queue` whose run was not active returns `keep_place` with a `mergeCallInFlight` flag; the queue position is preserved, and if a merge call may have been in flight (checked via the `merge_call` table in `mergeCallInFlight`) the merge job first asks GitHub whether that call went through before moving on (`src/core/recovery.ts:95-96`) (`src/db/remote-merges.ts:78-80`). If the run was still active in the lane, that item re-verifies instead (`src/core/recovery.ts:94-98`) (`src/core/recovery.test.ts:122-141`).
2. **Running/verifying items are resumed in a fresh session**, from their checkpoint or, without one, from the branch [E4:76-77,105]. If the runner still holds the item's work, the resume is marked `reattach: true` so it connects to the runner's ongoing work (the README confirms Paws "reattaches to the same commands after startup, including in-flight Closeout reviews and answer tasks" (`README.md:52-54`)).
3. **Verifying items re-verify.** A verifying item whose runner still holds its Closeout review or check run returns `reverify`, as does any item whose merge was in progress per its checkpoint, or a re-verify cut short by the restart (`src/core/recovery.ts:97-104`). `recoverOnStartup` only skips re-applying such a re-verify when it is already attached to the runner's open Closeout work (`src/db/recovery.ts:76-82`).
4. **Crash-loop protection.** If the item has already been resumed once (`recoveryAttempts >= 1`) and not enough time has passed since that resume (`sinceResumeMs < RESUME_AGAIN_AFTER_MS`), or if it has no checkpoint and has already been attempted once, Paws returns `ask_restart` instead of restarting automatically — per the doc comment, "the next start, still unfinished, asks in Linear whether to start it again" [E4:78-79,101-102] (`src/core/recovery.test.ts:111-120`), and `ensureRestartQuestion` is checked first so a standing restart question short-circuits the decision (`src/db/recovery.ts:58-61`).

`applyDecision` (src/db/decisions.ts) dispatches the concrete action per decision type: `resume` → `applyResume` (with a staggered `runAt` — recoverOnStartup spaces resumes 5 seconds apart via `STARTUP_RESUME_SPACING_MS`), `reverify` → `applyReverify`, `keep_place` → `applyKeepPlace`, `ask_restart` → `applyAskRestart` (`src/db/decisions.ts:21-48`) (`src/db/recovery.ts:39`).

Several guards skip decisions entirely for items that already have settled work pending: `hasParkedCapacityWait` (a pending capacity-wait job already exists for the item at its current version, in the running/recovering/verifying states and not cancel-requested, so restarting would spend recovery and add a duplicate job), `hasPendingAnswerResume`, and `hasPendingTransientRetry` [E1:62-64,103-114]. Before deciding anything, `shiftRunnerLeasesForDowntime` ensures Paws downtime up to `offlineBudgetMs` does not count against an open runner lease [E1:44,52].

For `awaiting_input` items specifically, recoverOnStartup does not resume them; it releases their run capacity and enqueues a one-off catchup job (`startup-questions`) so open questions are re-raised (`src/db/recovery.ts:89-98`).

A test, `test/startup-resume-stagger.test.ts`, exercises this: four items end up in `recovering` after a shutdown, then `recoverOnStartup` is called and resume jobs are observed being claimed while in-flight inspection is tracked so items are not double-handled (`test/startup-resume-stagger.test.ts:143-184`).

Running call and host infrastructure (JobLoop with 64 workers, 120s lease) continues polling the queue so the resumes and re-verifies actually get picked up after startup (`src/db/loops.ts:8-33`).

This is based on 18 source ranges in 16 files, and research stopped at the deep limit maxPasses, so other relevant code may not have been inspected.

applyResume, applyReverify, applyKeepPlace, and applyAskRestart bodies were not shown, so the exact side effects of each decision beyond 'creates/reuses jobs' are inferred from names and caller context.
